hint1.text: When enabled, an allow/deny permission prompt is first put to the {other} configured agents. Each judges the tool call from the recent context and votes allow/deny with a reason; the session's own agent then summarizes their opinions. If every voter agrees, the prompt auto-resolves with no human needed — otherwise you decide, with each agent's vote and reason shown. Any error, timeout, or unparseable answer counts as an abstain, which keeps the decision with you. Needs at least one agent besides the session's own.

hint2.text: {ask} (where the agent asks {you} a multiple-choice question) takes a separate per-question path. c3 always shows you an answer panel and injects your picks back to the agent — that is the only way to answer it without a terminal, so it works regardless of this toggle. The consensus part only kicks in when it's {on}: the voters answer every question and the decider summarizes and reconciles answers that mean the same thing, so questions everyone agrees on get pre-filled or auto-answered and only the rest are left for you. With consensus off, no voting runs and you fill the whole panel yourself.

proxy.hint: When enabled, the proxy URLs below are injected as HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars into every new session subprocess, and c3's own outbound requests — the update check and the release download — go through the same proxy. Loopback targets and NO_PROXY matches stay direct. Running sessions are not affected.

sessionCleanup.hint: Off by default. When enabled, a daily task deletes session transcripts older than the retention window from every agent session store on this machine — both the per-workspace sandbox homes and the host agent homes. Deleted sessions can no longer be resumed or viewed. Configuration, credential and skill files are never touched.

gitFailure.worktreeBranchOrPathTaken: The branch or worktree directory for this intent is still occupied — another worktree has it checked out, or a leftover branch/directory of the same name exists. Release or clean it up locally, then try again.
gitFailure.repoConflictUnresolved: The repository has unresolved merge conflicts, so Git refused this action. Finish resolving the conflicts (or abort the merge/rebase), then try again.
gitFailure.filesystemDenied: The local filesystem refused the write — no permission, read-only, or out of disk space. Check the disk space and the directory permissions, then try again.
gitFailure.forgeCliUnavailable: The forge CLI is not installed, or it is installed but not logged in. Install it and complete its login, then try again.
gitFailure.remotePermissionDenied: The remote rejected the request for lack of rights (push or PR creation). Ask for write access to the repository — or fix the credentials in use — then try again.
gitFailure.pushRejected: The push was rejected: the remote branch has moved ahead of your local one. Sync with the remote branch (pull/rebase and resolve any conflicts), then try again.
gitFailure.networkUnreachable: The remote or the forge API could not be reached (DNS, connection or timeout). Restore the network — check your proxy/VPN if you use one — then try again.
gitFailure.commitHookRejected: A commit/push hook or its lint-format chain rejected the change. Fix what the hook reported, then try again.
gitFailure.forgeCreateRejected: The forge refused to create the change request — its validation failed, or one already exists for this branch. Check the branch on the platform, fix what it objects to, then try again.

sdd.hint: When enabled, development tasks in this workspace go through a spec quality gate with human approval checkpoints before coding starts.

specRoot.hint: Fixed, centralized location where this project's specs are stored (~/.c3/specs/[project]). Shared by every worktree of the project and read-only — it cannot be changed here or via the API. Not committed to Git.

toggle.label: Allow machine approval of a passing spec review

machineApproval.hint: Off by default. When on, a spec whose read-only review concludes “pass” is approved by c3 itself, recorded under a machine identity that never impersonates a user, and development may start without a human click. The approval stays revocable — revoking returns the spec to “awaiting approval” and prevents the same review conclusion from being re-approved. Turning this off never revokes an already-approved spec.

maxFiles.hint: Upper bound on distinct changed files a fast-mode intent may produce in one manual turn. A diff reaching this many files is over the threshold and pins the intent back to sdd until a spec is authored and approved.

maxLines.hint: Upper bound on changed lines (additions + deletions) a fast-mode intent may produce in one manual turn. A binary change always counts as over.

gate.hint: Master switch for automatic dispatch in this workspace. When off, neither the cron tick loop nor event-triggered dispatchers start any automation; each automation's own active/paused state is left untouched and manual “run now” still works.

concurrency.hint: Upper bound on how many intents the automation queue drives in development at the same time (worktree isolation only). Spec authoring and review stay serial and never count, and manual starts are not limited by this cap. Default 2; lower values clamp to 1. Lowering the cap never cancels running sessions — it only pauses new auto-dispatch until occupancy drops below it.

hint1.text: When enabled, an allow/deny permission prompt is first put to the {other} configured agents. Each judges the tool call from the recent context and votes allow/deny with a reason; the session's own agent then summarizes their opinions. If every voter agrees, the prompt auto-resolves with no human needed — otherwise you decide, with each agent's vote and reason shown. Any error, timeout, or unparseable answer counts as an abstain, which keeps the decision with you. Needs at least one agent besides the session's own.

hint2.text: {ask} (where the agent asks {you} a multiple-choice question) takes a separate per-question path. c3 always shows you an answer panel and injects your picks back to the agent — that is the only way to answer it without a terminal, so it works regardless of this toggle. The consensus part only kicks in when it's {on}: the voters answer every question and the decider summarizes and reconciles answers that mean the same thing, so questions everyone agrees on get pre-filled or auto-answered and only the rest are left for you. With consensus off, no voting runs and you fill the whole panel yourself.

Everything else is hidden by default. c3 installs and version-pins the arapuca binary itself, falling back to one on the host PATH.
